recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-8793 follow-up source work is recommended unless a separate work-group decision revises the broader inter-version compatibility policy.
issue_request: FHIR-8793 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core clarification for the old history.html#rules section. It asked to change the overbroad statement that adding new elements in an existing resource is non-breaking so that only adding new optional elements is treated that way, while adding mandatory elements is recognized as a substantive change.
initial_application: The Jira comment records SVN revision 7967. In git, 62dc5f8590cd8e3569c35c1d3af86a20b5a5373f changed source/history.html from "adding new elements in an existing resource" to "adding new optional elements in an existing resource." The versioning-policy material was later reorganized into source/versions.html by d68b8964af6bcba886df7c89465a68e18951f5fd.
additional_context: The current source no longer uses the old history.html#rules section as the policy authority; source/history.html points to source/versions.html. Current source/versions.html defines inter-version change categories, says new optional elements may be introduced, and states minimum element cardinalities will not be changed for normative content. Later policy work such as FHIR-13089 expanded forward/backward compatibility guidance without contradicting the FHIR-8793 clarification. Targeted Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build source already implements the requested optional-versus-mandatory distinction, and adding duplicate wording to history.html would not correct a current specification problem.
